Stendhal, The Charterhouse of Parma, translated by C. K. Scott Moncrieff.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/stendhal/the-charterhouse-of-parma/c-k-scott-moncrieff

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Stendhal, the author, died 1842.
- C. K. Scott Moncrieff, the translator, died 1930.

First publication of the text used: 1925 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from French in 1925 by C. K. Scott Moncrieff.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1925, before 1931, so it is in the public domain in the United States. The edition's rights statement below says the same.
- Country of origin (not named in the facts; the translation is in English, so the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die, C. K. Scott Moncrieff (died 1930), means the translation is public domain in each of them from 1 January 2001 at the latest. The original French work by Stendhal is also public domain in every country, because its author died in 1925 or earlier.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
